note.note:
Action Plan:
1. Advise oral rehydration: increase fluid intake with clear fluids; recommend oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte), to be purchased over the counter.
2. Advise soft diet: recommend soft, easily digestible foods (e.g., soup, mash), and gradual reintroduction of solids as tolerated.
3. Continue symptomatic treatment: Paracetamol may be used for pain/fever (dose/route/frequency not documented).
4. Advise avoidance of alcohol during current illness.
5. Monitor symptoms: instruct patient to seek medical review if symptoms do not improve within 48 hours or if signs of dehydration develop.
6. Discussed red flag symptoms and provided safety netting (return if worsening, persistent vomiting, inability to keep fluids, blood in stools, or other concerns).
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Sudden onset of frequent, watery diarrhea for 3 days.
- Associated symptoms: Intermittent, crampy midline lower abdominal pain (approx. 6/10), nausea, occasional vomiting (noted especially after milk intake), subjective fever ("burning up"), mildly decreased urine frequency.
- No blood in stool.
- Otherwise able to keep fluids down; solid foods result in loose stool.
- Past medical history: No significant medical history; reports being otherwise fit and well.
- Medications: Recently used Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented); no regular medications.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Family history: Father with colon cancer (stage 3); no further detail.
- Social history: Lives with mother and sister; brother (not cohabiting) had similar diarrheal illness for 5 days (now improving); works in government office in Central London; social/occasional smoker; drinks alcohol on weekends and some weekdays, occasional binge drinking.
- No other sick contacts reported at home.

Objective:
- No in-person physical examination performed (virtual consult).
- No vital signs or formal temperature measurement available.
- No laboratory or imaging investigations performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute diarrheal illness:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute infectious gastroenteritis (High likelihood; DDx supported).
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Food poisoning (Medium likelihood; DDx supported; no clear food trigger recalled).
     - Secondary/transient lactase deficiency (Medium likelihood; vomiting after milk; DDx supported).
     - Inflammatory bowel disease (Low likelihood; DDx supported; acute onset and sick contact argue against).
     - Colorectal cancer (Very unlikely per DDx; age and acute course not typical, despite family history).
   - Investigations: None planned; advised monitoring unless symptoms worsen or persist.
   - Treatment: Oral rehydration with clear fluids and oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte); continue Paracetamol (for pain/fever); avoid alcohol; gradual dietary progression as tolerated.
   - Referral: Not indicated; review if no improvement or deterioration.

Quality checks:
● Missing/expected items:
   - No formal vital signs or physical exam findings (virtual setting); no documented assessment of hydration status beyond subjective report.
   - No medication reconciliation beyond Paracetamol.
   - No formal documentation of dietary intake apart from recent loose stools and vomiting after milk.
● Internal conflicts:
   - No conflicts identified between transcript and DDx.
● Transcript quality:
   - Generally clear; minimal irrelevant conversational noise; all clinically relevant information extractable.
